entries.punishment: Section 100 BNS is the definitional section: it defines culpable homicide as causing death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that the act is likely to cause death. It does not itself prescribe a penalty — punishment is provided under Section 105 BNS (culpable homicide not amounting to murder): where the act is done with intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine; where the act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death but without intention to cause death or such injury, imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, or fine, or both.
essentialIngredients: Death of a human being must be caused
Death must be caused by the accused's act (or omission amounting to an act in law)

The act must be done with one of the requisite mental states: (a) intention of causing death, OR (b) intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, OR (c) knowledge that the act is likely to cause death
There must be a causal connection (proximate cause) between the accused's act and the resulting death
The case must not fall within the added intention/knowledge and special aggravating conditions that would elevate it to murder under Section 101 BNS
